page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor operating at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. It is also capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong memory subsystem, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the top 25% at 32.9 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth reaches 453.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 85.02 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, cryptographic and vector-heavy operations show limitations; the Passmark CPU encryption test falls into the bottom 10%, and Geekbench ray tracing and image processing benchmarks are in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are also weak, with text generation on a 7B model reaching only 5.09 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio (1:8) and bundled local NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is appropriate for database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and general-purpose ARM64 development, provided the workloads do not rely heavily on complex cryptographic instructions or advanced vector extensions.
